question_this_answers: does the system do anything at all in a NEW ARBITRARY ENVIRONMENT, not a MiniWob page?

the_environment.name: MiniWob++ flight domain, Alaska app (mobile web)
the_environment.why_it_counts_as_new: real booking application markup, no #area, no #subbtn, no fixed 160x160 layout, no 'quoted' token in the goal, 139 elements, fields named SearchFields.DepartureCity etc., 60s episode instead of 10-15s
the_environment.note: the provided wrapper.html iframes index.html but the iframe never loads here (src stays '', contentDocument is about:blank); index.html was driven directly

measured_before.goal: Book a return flight from New York to Las Vegas, departing March 2 and returning March 24.
measured_before.interpretation: not a wrong action -- the system had nothing to say, on a page where all four values and all four controls were plainly present

measured_after.decompose: FILL_FORM with slots {origin: New York, destination: Las Vegas, depart: March 2, return: March 24}

what_was_added.SLOT_PATTERNS + slots(): goal_verb_decomposition_v1 reads (role, value) pairs out of an instruction. A sentence that names values but matches no known verb is a FORM FILL, not a refusal. This removes the single largest measured blindness.
what_was_added.v_fill_form: binds each slot to the control whose id/name/placeholder/class matches the ROLE, by name and not by order, then types and verifies.

two_instrument_faults_found_inside_this_: the first version clicked the field and typed into document.activeElement. On the Alaska page the click leaves activeElement as BODY, so the dates were never entered -- and the action string still said 'filled:depart=March 2'. Same defect class as every other one this session: an assertion that was never checked.

the correction asserts the focus target first, then verifies the value in the DOM afterwards, and falls back to setting it directly only if the keystrokes demonstrably did not land. A fill that cannot be read back is not counted as a fill.
what_is_NOT_claimed: that the flight task is SOLVED. Filling the search form is the first of several steps (select a departing flight, select a returning flight, complete the booking), and core.validateForm checks the whole trajectory. No flight episode was scored 1.0.
that this generalises. It is one page, one goal, one app.
that the sandbox can test live web apps. The browser has no outbound network: github.com renders title='' with 3 elements.
the_first_principles_reading: the system was not weak at learning; it was narrow at SEEING. It required #area, a 'quoted' token and a Submit button because those were the features of the benchmark it was built against. Remove that scaffolding and it produced nothing. The fix was not more learning -- it was a slot reader and a role-based binder, about 90 lines. That is the shape of the real limiting factor.
